localObjective.condition: Given points A and B on one force line of action
localObjective.criterion: explain that the force may move from A to B while direction, sense, and magnitude remain unchanged

contracts.modalityRationale: The proof requires a visible add-cancel-retain sequence; no new animation is produced.
contracts.misconceptionTarget: A force may be moved to a point outside its original line of action without changing its effect.
contracts.evidenceTarget: Name direction, sense, and magnitude as preserved, and state the same-line limitation.

math.expression: F_A ≡ F_B on one line of action
math.units: Qualitative figure; any force magnitude would be measured in newtons.
assumptions: A and B share one line of action
Direction, sense, and magnitude are unchanged

localObjective.condition: Given two concurrent forces of 80 N and 60 N and an included angle from 0 to 180 degrees
localObjective.criterion: determine the resultant magnitude and explain its maximum and minimum using the force parallelogram

contracts.modalityRationale: The chart compares resultant magnitude across the complete angle domain while retaining canonical Sim2 for vector manipulation.
contracts.misconceptionTarget: The resultant is always the scalar sum F1 + F2.
contracts.evidenceTarget: Identify and calculate the maximum at 0 degrees and minimum at 180 degrees.

math.expression: R = sqrt(F1^2 + F2^2 + 2 F1 F2 cos(theta))
math.units: F1, F2, and R in newtons; theta in degrees.

localObjective.condition: Given an incline angle beta and friction coefficient mu
localObjective.criterion: classify equilibrium or slip by comparing beta with phi = arctan(mu) and locating the resultant reaction relative to the friction cone

contracts.modalityRationale: The focused surface mounts canonical Sim2 so learners can cross the beta equals phi boundary without duplicate physics.
contracts.misconceptionTarget: Friction always has magnitude mu times N below the limiting state.
contracts.evidenceTarget: Predict and verify equilibrium or slip from beta compared with phi.

math.expression: tan(phi) = mu; slip iff beta > phi
math.units: beta and phi in degrees; mu dimensionless.

localObjective.condition: Given a 6 cm by 4 cm plate with a radius 1 cm circular hole centered at (4.5 cm, 2.5 cm)
localObjective.criterion: calculate the remaining centroid with signed areas and predict the direction of its shift before the final arithmetic

contracts.modalityRationale: Step control separates signed area, signed moments, and final coordinates while reusing the canonical centroid helper.
contracts.misconceptionTarget: Subtracting hole coordinates after averaging produces the remaining centroid.
contracts.evidenceTarget: Use a negative hole area, form both signed first moments, and predict movement away from removed material.

math.expression: xC = sum(Ai xi)/sum(Ai); yC = sum(Ai yi)/sum(Ai), with Ahole < 0
math.units: Coordinates in centimeters; areas in square centimeters.
